title: Line and rotational symmetry
goal: I can find lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry.
teach: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that are mirror images; if you fold on it, the halves match. A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than 360°. The order is the number of times it fits onto itself in one full turn. A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry and order n.

ex.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have, and what is its order of rotational symmetry?
steps: 3 lines go through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides: 6 lines.
It fits onto itself 6 times in a full turn: order 6.

watch: The diagonals of a rectangle are not lines of symmetry: folding on one does not match the halves.

qs.text: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order n.
2. An equilateral triangle is regular with n = 3.
3. So it has 3 lines of symmetry.

qs.text: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have?
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a line of symmetry is a fold line where both halves match exactly.
2. Only the fold from the top corner down the middle makes the halves match.
3. So it has 1 line of symmetry.

qs.text: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a rectangle?
qs.steps:
1. Rule: the order of rotational symmetry is how many times a shape fits onto itself in one full turn.
2. A rectangle fits onto itself after a half turn (180°) and after a full turn (360°).
3. So the order is 2.
